recipes.subtitleEn: 一锅可做 · 90ml (3fl oz) extra-virgin olive oil · 2 onions, finely sliced
recipes.detailsZh: Frittata di spaghetti以90ml (3fl oz) extra-virgin olive oil、2 onions, finely sliced、4 courgettes (zucchini), cut into 1cm (1⁄2in) rounds、250g (9oz) dried spaghetti为主要材料，偏家常做法，步骤完整，更适合作为午晚餐主菜或搭配主食。
recipes.detailsEn: Frittata di spaghetti以90ml (3fl oz) extra-virgin olive oil、2 onions, finely sliced、4 courgettes (zucchini), cut into 1cm (1⁄2in) rounds、250g (9oz) dried spaghetti为主要材料，偏家常做法，步骤完整，更适合作为午晚餐主菜或搭配主食。
materialsZh: sea salt and freshly ground black pepper
materialsEn: sea salt and freshly ground black pepper
stepsZh: Preheat the oven to 200°C/180°C fan/400°F/Gas 6.
Heat 2 tablespoons of the olive oil in a large, ovenproof, non-stick frying pan over a medium heat. Add the onions and cook them for 5 minutes, until softening but not fully cooked.

Add the courgettes (zucchini) and fry them for a further 15 minutes over a low heat, until the onions and courgettes are very soft and slightly caramelized. Tip the mixture into a large bowl and leave it all to one side.
Meanwhile, bring a large pan of salted water to a boil. Add the spaghetti and cook it fully according to the packet instructions.
Drain the pasta in a colander and leave it to cool, tossing through 1 tablespoon of the remaining olive oil so that the pasta doesn’t stick together.
Add the beaten eggs, parmesan and basil to the cooked onion and courgette and stir everything to combine, then tip in the spaghetti. Mix well, then season with salt and pepper.

Heat 2 tablespoons of the remaining olive oil in a large nonstick frying pan over a low heat. When the oil is hot, pour in the frittata mixture and push it down with a wooden spoon to ensure the mixture fills the pan in an even layer.
Leave the frittata to cook for 5 minutes, then shake the pan a little to loosen it.

Place a large plate on top of the pan and cover it with a tea towel. Holding the tea towel and plate firmly with the palm of one hand, hold the pan handle with the other hand and flip the pan over to invert the frittata on to the plate.
Place the frying pan back on the heat and add the remaining olive oil. Then, slide the frittata, uncooked-side down, back into the hot pan.
Cook it for a further 5 minutes over a low heat, then transfer the pan to the hot oven for 5 minutes to cook the frittata through.
Slide the frittata onto a board, then serve it sliced into wedges. It’s excellent for a picnic – allow it to cool then slice and wrap the slices to transport.

recipes.detailsZh: Honey ice cream以500ml (17fl oz) whole milk、500ml (17fl oz) double (heavy) cream、4 egg yolks、100g (31⁄2oz) caster (superfine) sugar为主要材料，偏家常做法，步骤完整，更适合作为午晚餐主菜或搭配主食。
recipes.detailsEn: Honey ice cream以500ml (17fl oz) whole milk、500ml (17fl oz) double (heavy) cream、4 egg yolks、100g (31⁄2oz) caster (superfine) sugar为主要材料，偏家常做法，步骤完整，更适合作为午晚餐主菜或搭配主食。
materialsZh: 100g (31⁄2oz) runny honey, plus extra for drizzling
materialsEn: 100g (31⁄2oz) runny honey, plus extra for drizzling
stepsZh: Heat the milk and cream together in a small saucepan over a low–medium heat, until they just reach a simmer. Turn off the heat.
In a large bowl, whisk together the egg yolks and sugar for 5 minutes, until they are pale in colour.
Take a ladleful of the hot milk and cream mixture and whisk this into the eggs and sugar.
Once they are well combined, slowly pour in the rest of the hot milk and cream, whisking at a gentle pace the whole time, making sure the two come together fully into a thin custard.
Pour the custard mixture back into the cream pan and place the pan over a low heat. Using a wooden spoon, stir slowly for about 8 minutes, until the mixture thickens to coat the back of the spoon.

Remove the pan from the heat and whisk in the honey. Pour the ice-cream mixture into a bowl and put it on top of a tray of ice, so that it cools down quickly. Stir the mixture occasionally to release the heat.
Once the ice-cream mixture is cold, transfer it to the fridge for at least 3 hours, or preferably overnight, to chill fully.

Pour the mixture into an ice-cream machine and churn it according to the manufacturer’s instructions, until thick. Spoon the mixture into a freezerproof container and pop on the lid. Place the ice cream in the freezer until fully set.
Alternatively, follow the instructions in the introduction above. Serve in chilled bowls with extra honey drizzled on top.

recipes.subtitleEn: 一锅可做 · 250g (9oz) ricotta · 4 eggs, separated
recipes.detailsZh: Honey, almond and ricotta cake以250g (9oz) ricotta、4 eggs, separated、2 tablespoons runny honey、1 teaspoon vanilla extract为主要材料，偏家常做法，步骤完整，更适合作为午晚餐主菜或搭配主食。
recipes.detailsEn: Honey, almond and ricotta cake以250g (9oz) ricotta、4 eggs, separated、2 tablespoons runny honey、1 teaspoon vanilla extract为主要材料，偏家常做法，步骤完整，更适合作为午晚餐主菜或搭配主食。
stepsZh: Preheat the oven to 180°C/160°C fan/350°F/Gas 4. Grease a 22cm (81⁄2in) cake tin with butter.

Put the ricotta, egg yolks, honey, vanilla, chopped almonds, baking powder and orange zest in a large mixing bowl and beat with a hand-held electric mixer, until you have a smooth, soft, light texture. (You can do this with a balloon whisk, if you prefer.)

In a separate, clean bowl, whisk the egg whites to soft peaks, then fold a spoonful of the whites into the ricotta mixture to loosen it a little. Gently fold in the remaining egg whites until no streaks remain. Don’t overmix.
Pour the cake mixture into the prepared cake tin and scatter the flaked (slivered) almonds evenly over the top.
Bake the cake for 30 minutes, or until a skewer inserted into the centre comes out clean (if the skewer isn’t clean after 30 minutes, return the cake to the oven and bake for 5 minutes more).
Remove the cake from the oven and leave it to cool in the tin on a wire rack.

Once the cake is cool, remove it from the tin and transfer it to a serving plate. Dust with icing (confectioner’s) sugar and serve the cake as a dessert with sweet wine, or with a coffee as an afternoon pick-me-up.

recipes.subtitleZh: 一锅可做 · 200g (7oz) 70% dark (bittersweet) chocolate, broken into pieces · 150g (51⁄2oz) unsalted butter, chopped
recipes.subtitleEn: 一锅可做 · 200g (7oz) 70% dark (bittersweet) chocolate, broken into pieces · 150g (51⁄2oz) unsalted butter, chopped
recipes.detailsZh: Honey, chestnut and chocolate torte以200g (7oz) 70% dark (bittersweet) chocolate, broken into pieces、150g (51⁄2oz) unsalted butter, chopped、300g (101⁄2oz) chestnut spread ( crème de marrons )、6 eggs, separated为主要材料，偏家常做法，步骤完整，更适合作为午晚餐主菜或搭配主食。
recipes.detailsEn: Honey, chestnut and chocolate torte以200g (7oz) 70% dark (bittersweet) chocolate, broken into pieces、150g (51⁄2oz) unsalted butter, chopped、300g (101⁄2oz) chestnut spread ( crème de marrons )、6 eggs, separated为主要材料，偏家常做法，步骤完整，更适合作为午晚餐主菜或搭配主食。
stepsZh: Preheat the oven to 180°C/160°C fan/350°F/Gas 4. Line the base and sides of a 24cm (91⁄2in) cake tin with baking paper.

Place the chocolate and butter into a heatproof bowl over a pan of simmering water (don’t let the bottom of the bowl touch the water). Once the chocolate and butter have melted, stir the two together and remove the bowl from the pan.
Leave to cool for a couple of minutes, then whisk in the chestnut spread, egg yolks and honey until fully combined. Set aside.
In a separate, clean bowl, whisk the egg whites so that they hold soft peaks.
Carefully fold one quarter of the egg whites into the chocolate, honey and chestnut mixture. When mixed, fold in the rest of the egg whites, keeping the mixture as aerated as possible.

Pour the mixture evenly into the lined cake tin and bake the cake for 45 minutes, or until a skewer inserted into the centre comes out clean. Remove from the oven and transfer the cake in the tin to a wire rack to cool completely.
Turn out the cooled cake and place it on a flat serving plate. Dust the top with icing (confectioner’s) sugar and serve with a glass of vin santo.
stepsEn: Preheat the oven to 180°C/160°C fan/350°F/Gas 4. Line the base and sides of a 24cm (91⁄2in) cake tin with baking paper.

Place the chocolate and butter into a heatproof bowl over a pan of simmering water (don’t let the bottom of the bowl touch the water). Once the chocolate and butter have melted, stir the two together and remove the bowl from the pan.
Leave to cool for a couple of minutes, then whisk in the chestnut spread, egg yolks and honey until fully combined. Set aside.
In a separate, clean bowl, whisk the egg whites so that they hold soft peaks.
Carefully fold one quarter of the egg whites into the chocolate, honey and chestnut mixture. When mixed, fold in the rest of the egg whites, keeping the mixture as aerated as possible.

Pour the mixture evenly into the lined cake tin and bake the cake for 45 minutes, or until a skewer inserted into the centre comes out clean. Remove from the oven and transfer the cake in the tin to a wire rack to cool completely.
Turn out the cooled cake and place it on a flat serving plate. Dust the top with icing (confectioner’s) sugar and serve with a glass of vin santo.
notesZh: Serves 8
notesEn: Serves 8

recipes.detailsZh: Lasagne with pesto and potatoes以300g (101⁄2oz) green beans, trimmed, then halved、4 Désirée or Cyprus potatoes, peeled and cut into 5mm (1⁄4in) slices、1 tablespoon extra-virgin olive oil、300g (101⁄2oz) egg-based dried lasagne为主要材料，偏家常做法，步骤完整，更适合作为午晚餐主菜或搭配主食。

materialsZh: 4 Désirée or Cyprus potatoes, peeled and cut into 5mm (1⁄4in) slices
1⁄2 garlic clove, crushed to a paste with a little sea salt
500ml (17fl oz) whole milk, warmed to just below boiling point
materialsEn: 4 Désirée or Cyprus potatoes, peeled and cut into 5mm (1⁄4in) slices
1⁄2 garlic clove, crushed to a paste with a little sea salt
500ml (17fl oz) whole milk, warmed to just below boiling point
stepsZh: Preheat the oven to 200°C/180°C fan/400°F/Gas 6.
First, make the pesto. Crush the garlic and the basil leaves in a pestle and mortar until the leaves become a pulp. Tip in the pine nuts and crush these to a paste, too.

Add the parmesan followed by 2 tablespoons of water, continuing to crush and mix so that everything comes together. Add the olive oil in a thin stream, mixing as you go, then set the pesto to one side.

Now prepare the béchamel. Melt the butter in a medium saucepan over a low heat. Add the flour and cook for 3 minutes, stirring with a wooden spoon. Slowly add the hot milk, stirring continuously to avoid any lumps forming.
When you have added all the milk, leave the sauce to cook over a low heat for 15 minutes, gently stirring throughout, until smooth and thickened. Remove the sauce from the heat and leave it to cool.
When cool, stir in half the pesto, then leave the sauce to one side.
Bring a large saucepan of salted water to a boil over a high heat. Add the green beans, bring the water back to a boil and boil them for 5 minutes, until soft to the bite.
Using a slotted spoon, remove the beans from the pan and leave them to cool.

Add the potato slices to the boiling water and cook them for 3 minutes, then drain and leave the potatoes to cool in the colander (do not rinse with cold water as the cooked potatoes will absorb the water, which you don’t want).
Grease a baking dish with the olive oil, then place a thin layer of the béchamel and pesto sauce in the base of the dish.
Next add a thin layer of potatoes and a scattering of green beans, then sprinkle over about 1 tablespoon of grated parmesan and cover with a layer of pasta. Repeat this so you have three layers.
Then, finish with a layer of lasagne sheets, a final layer of pesto-béchamel sauce and a layer of potaotes on top. Sprinkle the top with some more parmesan and cover the dish with foil.
Bake the lasagne for 45 minutes, then remove the foil and bake for a further 10 minutes, so the top of the lasagne gets a little colour and the edges crisp up.
Remove the dish from the oven and leave the lasagne to stand for 10 minutes before you serve it with the remaining pesto drizzled on top, extra parmesan grated over and a few grinds of black pepper.

stepsZh: Mix the zest and juice together in a small bowl and keep to one side.

stepsZh: Preheat the oven to 200°C/180°C fan/400°F/Gas 6.

Pour the icing over the top of the cooled cake in an even layer, then leave it to set for 1 hour. Serve in slices with a cup of tea.

recipes.detailsZh: Mushroom and ricotta ravioli以For the pasta dough、350g (12oz) tipo OO flour、25g (1oz) fine semolina flour, plus 50g (13⁄4oz) for dusting、4 egg yolks为主要材料，偏家常做法，步骤完整，更适合作为午晚餐主菜或搭配主食。

materialsZh: 25g (1oz) fine semolina flour, plus 50g (13⁄4oz) for dusting
30g (1oz) dried porcini mushrooms, just covered in boiling water and left to soak
100g (31⁄2oz) parmesan, grated, plus extra to serve
sea salt and freshly ground black pepper
1 garlic clove, crushed to a paste with a little sea salt
materialsEn: 25g (1oz) fine semolina flour, plus 50g (13⁄4oz) for dusting
30g (1oz) dried porcini mushrooms, just covered in boiling water and left to soak
100g (31⁄2oz) parmesan, grated, plus extra to serve
sea salt and freshly ground black pepper
1 garlic clove, crushed to a paste with a little sea salt
stepsZh: First make the pasta dough. Place all the dough ingredients in a food processor (or mix and knead by hand) and pulse the mixture for 3 minutes, until you have lots of small balls of dough.
If the dough seems dry, add 2 tablespoons of water and blend again. Tip the dough into a bowl and squeeze it together into a big ball.
Divide the dough into 4 equal pieces, wrap each in cling film (plastic wrap) and place the balls in the fridge for 30 minutes to rest while you make the filling.
To make the filling, heat the olive oil in a large nonstick frying pan over a medium heat.

When hot, add the portobellos and cook them for 10 minutes – the mushrooms will release a lot of water, but leave that in the pan and cook the mushrooms down until they go syrupy. Reserving the soaking liquid, add the porcini to the pan.
Then, using a coffee filter to prevent any grit going into your sauce, pour in the soaking liquid too. Cook for a further 5 minutes, then tip the mushrooms into a large bowl and leave them to cool.
Chop the cooled mushrooms very finely so they are almost a paste, then return them to the bowl and add the ricotta, parmesan, parsley and egg.

Mix thoroughly and season well with salt and pepper – the flavour will slightly dilute once the filling is covered in fresh pasta, so do be generous with the seasoning. Set the filling aside while you make the sauce.
To make the sauce, pour the hot water into a large frying pan and bring it to a simmer over a medium heat. Add the spinach and cook for about 1 minute, until wilted, then tip it into a colander.

Using a wooden spoon, squeeze out any excess water then take a few sheets of kitchen paper and push down on the spinach so that it is as dry as possible. Place the spinach on a chopping board and roughly chop.

Wipe out the frying pan with some kitchen paper and place it back over a medium heat. Add the cream and garlic and bring the cream to a simmer. Add the chopped spinach, and turn off the heat. Leave to one side while you roll the pasta.
Using a rolling pin, roll 1 of the 4 portions of pasta until the dough is thin enough to go through the rollers in your pasta machine at its widest setting.
Place one end of the flattened dough into the machine and roll the pasta through the machine. Fold the sheet in half and roll again.
Repeat this process 4 times for each portion of pasta – it makes the pasta more elastic, so it will be much more durable and won’t break.
When you have prepared all the portions of pasta in this way, you can start making the ravioli.
First, transfer the filling to a large piping bag with a large plain nozzle, or simply use a spoon to scoop the filling from the bowl.
Using your pasta machine, roll out each pasta portion as thinly as you can. Place one sheet on a lightly floured work surface and dust it with some extra flour to stop it sticking.
Work along the centre of the length of the pasta sheet, piping or spooning 1 teaspoon of filling at regular intervals along the sheet – aim for a 2-fingerwidth space between each dollop.
Using a pastry brush, brush water in between the mounds of filling and all along the edges of the pasta sheet. Carefully fold over the length of the pasta sheet, encasing the filling.

Using your fingertips, gently press the long edges of the pasta sheet together and cup your hand and push down on the ravioli to remove unwanted air pockets. Repeat with the remaining pasta sheets and filling.

Using a zig-zag pasta cutter, slice between each pocket of filled pasta to cut the individual ravioli. Give a tray a good dusting of semolina flour and transfer the ravioli to the tray as you go. Leave the ravioli to rest for 1 hour.
When you’re ready to cook the ravioli, place the frying pan with the sauce back on the hob over a low heat.
Bring a large saucepan of salted water to a boil over a high heat. Add the ravioli and when they rise to the top of the water, cook them for a further 2 minutes, until tender.
Using a slotted spoon, transfer the ravioli from the water into the pan with the sauce.

recipes.titleEn: Neapolitan rum and Amalfi lemon baba
recipes.subtitleZh: 一锅可做 · 2 tablespoons whole milk · 5g (1⁄8oz) dried yeast
recipes.subtitleEn: 一锅可做 · 2 tablespoons whole milk · 5g (1⁄8oz) dried yeast
recipes.detailsZh: Neapolitan rum and Amalfi lemon baba以2 tablespoons whole milk、5g (1⁄8oz) dried yeast、500g (1lb 2oz) strong white bread flour, plus extra for flouring、60g (21⁄4oz) caster (superfine) sugar为主要材料，偏家常做法，步骤完整，更适合作为午晚餐主菜或搭配主食。

materialsZh: 500g (1lb 2oz) strong white bread flour, plus extra for flouring
180g (61⁄4oz) butter, cubed, plus extra for greasing
materialsEn: 500g (1lb 2oz) strong white bread flour, plus extra for flouring

stepsZh: Mix the milk and yeast together in a medium bowl and add 2 heaped tablespoons of the strong white bread flour, combining to a smooth dough.
Position the dough in the middle of the bowl, cover it with cling film (plastic wrap) and keep it in a warm place for 30 minutes.

In a stand mixer fitted with the dough hook, add the remaining flour to the mixing bowl and then add the risen yeast, milk and flour mixture. Turn on the mixer at its lowest setting, then steadily add the sugar.
Next add the eggs, one at a time, allowing each egg to be incorporated before adding another. After about 10 minutes, the mixture should be smooth and well combined.
At that point, add the salt and then, one at a time, add the cubes of butter.

Once you’ve added all the butter, continue mixing on a low speed for 3 minutes, until the dough is smooth and elastic. Take the bowl off the machine and cover it in cling film. Leave it in a warm place for 2 hours for the dough to rise.

While the dough is rising, make the sugar syrup. Pour 1 litre (35fl oz) of water into a large saucepan. Add the sugar and place the pan over a medium heat. Bring the syrup to a boil, then turn down the heat to a simmer.
Add the lemon zest and simmer for 15 minutes, then turn off the heat. Leave the syrup to cool, then add the rum. Transfer the syrup to a container and place it in the fridge until needed.
Grease (with butter) and flour each baba mould, then set the moulds aside.

Tip out the risen dough on to a lightly floured work surface. Use your hands to knock it back to release the air pockets in the dough. Cut the dough into roughly 80g (3oz) pieces and roll each piece into a ball.
Place one dough ball into each baba mould and leave them in a warm place for about 20 minutes, until the dough has reached the top of each mould.
While the babas are rising, preheat the oven to 200°C/180°C fan/400°F/Gas 6.
Place the babas on a baking sheet and into the oven. Bake them for 30 minutes, until golden, then turn out the babas on to a wire rack to cool.

While the babas are baking, make the crema di mascarpone. In a bowl, whisk the mascarpone with the icing (confectioner’s) sugar and marsala. Add the cream and scrape in the vanilla seeds from the pod.
Whisk again until the mixture is smooth and holds soft peaks. Set aside until you’re ready to serve.
While the babas are cooling, pour the syrup back into a saucepan and reheat it over a low heat.
Using tongs, dip each baba into the warm syrup and then turn it right side up back on to the wire rack. (Place a tray underneath the rack to catch the drips.) Reserve the remaining syrup to serve.
Serve the babas with crema di mascarpone and the remaining syrup, and topped with a piece of the Amalfi lemon peel.

recipes.detailsZh: Passatelli in broth以For the broth、4 chicken drumsticks or wings、2 carrots, peeled and roughly chopped、2 celery stalks, roughly chopped为主要材料，偏家常做法，步骤完整，更适合作为午晚餐主菜或搭配主食。

materialsZh: 200g (7oz) parmesan, grated, plus extra to serve
sea salt and freshly ground black pepper
materialsEn: 200g (7oz) parmesan, grated, plus extra to serve
sea salt and freshly ground black pepper
stepsZh: First, make the broth. Place all ingredients into a large saucepan with 3 litres (105fl oz) of cold water and place the pan over a high heat.
Bring the liquid to a boil, skimming off any foam as it rises to the top, then turn down the heat and leave the broth to simmer for 60 minutes to develop its flavour.

Remove the chicken and the vegetables with a slotted spoon, then pour the broth through a fine sieve into a clean saucepan. Set aside. (Keep the chicken meat for a chicken sandwich and discard the bones and the veg.)
To make the passatelli, mix the breadcrumbs, parmesan and eggs in a large bowl, then add a little grating of nutmeg (not too much) and the lemon zest.
Mix everything together with your hands and work the dough so that it becomes tight and elastic.
Shape the dough into a ball then wrap it in cling film (plastic wrap) and rest it in the fridge for 30 minutes – this will help the passatelli hold together during cooking.
Meanwhile, grab a baking sheet or tray and lightly dust it with flour. Cut the chilled dough into quarters and roll each quarter into a ball.
Place each ball into a potato ricer that has large holes, then push down the handle and let the passatelli fall through the holes into the floured tray below.
Repeat until you have used all the dough, then place the tray of passatelli in the fridge for 30 minutes.

Bring the broth to a simmer over a medium heat, then carefully drop in the passatelli. Cook until the passatelli rise to the surface of the broth. Remove from the heat and serve in hot bowls with a little extra parmesan on top.

recipes.titleZh: Pine nut and caramel ice cream
recipes.titleEn: Pine nut and caramel ice cream
recipes.subtitleZh: 一锅可做 · 500ml (17fl oz) whole milk · 500ml (17fl oz) double (heavy) cream
recipes.subtitleEn: 一锅可做 · 500ml (17fl oz) whole milk · 500ml (17fl oz) double (heavy) cream
recipes.detailsZh: Pine nut and caramel ice cream以500ml (17fl oz) whole milk、500ml (17fl oz) double (heavy) cream、1 vanilla pod, split lengthways、4 egg yolks为主要材料，偏家常做法，步骤完整，更适合作为午晚餐主菜或搭配主食。
recipes.detailsEn: Pine nut and caramel ice cream以500ml (17fl oz) whole milk、500ml (17fl oz) double (heavy) cream、1 vanilla pod, split lengthways、4 egg yolks为主要材料，偏家常做法，步骤完整，更适合作为午晚餐主菜或搭配主食。
stepsZh: Pour the milk and cream into a large, heavy-based saucepan and add the vanilla pod. Place the pan over a low–medium heat and warm through until the mixture just reaches a simmer.
Remove the split pod and scrape out the vanilla seeds into the pan, then turn off the heat.

In a large bowl, whisk the egg yolks and sugar together for 5 minutes, until they are pale in colour. Take a ladleful of the hot milk and cream mixture and whisk this into the egg mixture until combined.
Slowly pour in the remainder of the warmed milk and cream mixture, whisking gently the whole time until you have a thin custard.
Pour the mixture back into the saucepan then place the pan over a low heat. Stir slowly with a wooden spoon for about 8 minutes, until the mixture thickens enough to coat the back of the spoon.

Pour the custard into a bowl and place the bowl on a tray of ice, so that the mixture cools quickly. Stir occasionally to release the heat. Transfer the bowl to the fridge and chill for at least 3 hours, or ideally overnight.
Meanwhile make the pine nut caramel. Preheat the oven to 200°C/180°C fan/400°F/Gas 6. Grease a silicone baking mat or stainless-steel baking tray with a little oil.
Scatter the pine nuts evenly over a shallow baking tray and roast them in the oven for 3 minutes, until golden. Remove from the oven and leave to cool.
Tip the sugar into a small saucepan with 1 tablespoon of water. Place the pan over a low heat and leave the sugar to dissolve. Do not stir.
When the sugar is a light straw colour, add the roasted pine nuts, and stir them through the syrup very gently with a wooden spoon.
Continue to cook over a low heat, until the caramel is light golden – at this point, quickly take the pan off the heat and pour the mixture on to the greased silicone sheet or stainless-steel tray.
Leave the caramel to cool down completely and harden.

Once it has cooled and hardened, use your hands to break up the caramel into pieces, then place them into a large Ziplock bag. Using a rolling pin, bash the caramel in the bag to create a fine crumb – this will take about 5 minutes.

When you’re ready to churn the ice cream, pour the cooled custard into your ice-cream machine and churn it according to the manufacturer’s instructions, until thick. Spoon the ice cream into a freezerproof container and pop on a lid.
Transfer the container to the freezer until semi-set.

Set aside a few tablespoons of the pine nut caramel mixture to use as garnish later, and stir the remainder through the ice cream in the container until you have distributed it evenly. Return the ice cream to the freezer until set.
Serve the ice cream in chilled bowls sprinkled with the reserved pine nut caramel to decorate.

150g (51⁄2oz) unsalted butter, cut into small cubes

stepsZh: In a large bowl, mix together the flour, baking powder, toasted pine nuts, salt and rosemary. Add the cubes of butter and work them in with your fingertips until combined.

In a separate bowl, whisk the egg, then add the milk and stir again so they are well combined. Pour the egg and milk mixture into the flour and butter mixture and add the parmesan. Mix everything well and bring it together into a dough.

Tip out the dough on to a lightly floured work surface. Using a rolling pin, roll out the dough until it is 1cm (1⁄2in) thick, then fold it in half. Repeat this rolling and folding 4 times – this helps the dough to become more elastic.
Shape the dough into a square, wrap it in cling film (plastic wrap), then refrigerate it for 20 minutes to rest.
Meanwhile, preheat the oven to 200°C/180°C fan/400°F/Gas 6. Line a baking sheet with baking paper.

Roll out the chilled dough on a lightly floured work surface until it is 5mm (1⁄4in) thick. Using a medium, round cookie cutter, cut out as many biscuits as possible, re-rolling the trimmings as necessary.
Gently transfer the biscuits to the lined baking sheet (a palette knife is good for this). Brush a little milk over the tops, add a sprinkling of grated parmesan to each biscuit and a few pine nuts.
Bake the biscuits in the oven for 20 minutes, then transfer them to a wire rack to cool. Serve as a cheese biscuit with a selection of Italian cheeses.

materialsZh: 100g (31⁄2oz) unsalted butter, softened at room temperature
150g (51⁄2oz) tipo OO flour (or chickpea/gram flour if you’re gluten intolerant)
materialsEn: 100g (31⁄2oz) unsalted butter, softened at room temperature
150g (51⁄2oz) tipo OO flour (or chickpea/gram flour if you’re gluten intolerant)
stepsZh: First make the ’nduja butter. Put the butter in a ceramic bowl and beat it with a wooden spoon until it is really creamy. Add the ’nduja (it’s important this is at room temperature) and the rosemary and mix to a smooth paste.
Set aside while you make the polenta.
Pour 400ml (14fl oz) of water into a medium saucepan and place it over a high heat. Bring it to a boil, add a pinch of salt and bring the water back to a simmer.

Reduce the heat so that the water is simmering gently and slowly pour in the bramata polenta, stirring with a balloon whisk the whole time – slow is the key here, so that you disperse the polenta evenly in the water.
Once you have added all the polenta, turn down the heat and cook the polenta gently for 30 minutes, until it is starting to come away from the edges of the pan.
Immediately pour the polenta into a straight-sided ceramic dish so that it’s 2cm (3⁄4in) thick. Leave to cool and set firm. Slice the cooled, set polenta into 2 × 4cm (3⁄4 × 11⁄2in) pieces.
Pour the milk into a wide, shallow bowl and the flour into another.
One by one, dip the polenta pieces first into the milk and then into the flour, making sure each is fully coated. Set each aside on a plate while you coat the remainder.
Pour the sunflower oil into a small, heavy-based saucepan and place it over a high heat.

When it reaches 170°C/325°F on a cooking thermometer (or when a small piece of polenta dropped into the oil sizzles and turns golden within a few seconds), carefully place a few of the polenta pieces in the hot oil (no more than 4 at a time).

Deep-fry them for about 3 minutes, until they are a light golden colour all over. Remove them using a slotted spoon and transfer them to a wire rack set over a tray to drain. Fry the remaining polenta pieces.
Sprinkle the warm fingers with flaky sea salt and serve with the ’nduja butter in little bowls alongside for dunking.

stepsZh: Pour 400ml (14fl oz) of water into a medium saucepan, salt the water and bring it to a boil over a high heat. Add the fennel slices, bring the water back to a boil and boil the fennel for 3 minutes, until tender.
Remove the pieces with a slotted spoon and set them aside.
Add 75ml (21⁄4fl oz) of water to the saucepan (this is to allow for the water that has evaporated in cooking the fennel), then bring it back to a boil.

Reduce the heat so that the water is simmering gently and slowly stir in the bramata polenta, stirring with a balloon whisk the whole time – slow is the key here, so that you disperse the polenta evenly in the water.

Once you have added all the polenta, turn down the heat and cook it gently for 30 minutes, until it is starting to come away from the edges of the pan. Add 2 tablespoons of the olive oil, and season with salt and pepper if needed.
Keep the polenta warm until you’re ready to serve.
Heat the remaining olive oil in a small frying pan over a medium heat. Add the cooked fennel slices and cook them gently for 3 minutes, then add the garlic, parsley, chilli and all the crab meat.
Cook very gently for 3 minutes, then add the lemon juice and check the seasoning.

Place a generous spoonful of wet polenta on to each serving plate and divide the cooked crab and fennel equally over the top. Toss a few rocket (arugula) leaves in a little olive oil, and use these to garnish the top of each dish.Serve straightaway.

recipes.detailsZh: Polenta, pistachio and orange cake以200g (7oz) pistachio kernels, finely ground – use a spice grinder or food processor、zest and juice of 1 orange、200g (7oz) bramata polenta、4 eggs为主要材料，偏家常做法，步骤完整，更适合作为午晚餐主菜或搭配主食。

materialsEn: 200g (7oz) pistachio kernels, finely ground – use a spice grinder or food processor

stepsZh: Preheat the oven to 200°C/180°C fan/400°F/Gas 6. Grease a 24cm (10in) springform cake tin with oil, and line the base with baking paper.
In a large bowl, mix the ground pistachios, orange zest and the polenta together. Crack the eggs into another bowl and whisk in the honey, orange juice and olive oil until smooth.
Pour the wet mixture into the dry and thoroughly combine to a smooth batter, then pour the batter into the prepared tin.
Bake the cake for 40 minutes, until a skewer inserted into the centre comes out clean, then remove the cake from the oven and transfer it to a wire rack to cool in the tin.
Once the cake is cool, release it from the tin and transfer it to a large plate.

To make the syrup, stir the orange juice and honey together in a small saucepan. Place the pan over a medium–low heat and bring the ingredients to a simmer, stirring to fully combine. Immediately remove the syrup from the heat.
Using a fine skewer, prick a few holes into the top of the cake and pour the honey and orange syrup over the top. Sprinkle on the orange zest and pistachios to decorate.

20g (3⁄4oz) dried porcini mushrooms, just covered in boiling water and left to soak, drained and finely chopped
1⁄2 garlic clove, crushed to a paste with a little sea salt
sea salt and freshly ground black pepper
materialsEn: about 1.5 litres (52fl oz) hot vegetable stock (homemade)

stepsZh: Bring a pan of salted water to a boil over a high heat. Add the spinach, stir it for 10 seconds, then drain it in a colander. Squeeze it with a pair of tongs until there is no more excess water, then chop it finely and leave it to one side.
To make the risotto, heat the olive oil in a straight-sided saucepan over a medium heat. Add the onion and celery and cook it gently for 2 minutes, then add the carnaroli rice.

Cook it for a further 3 minutes, stirring continuously, then add the white wine. A couple of ladlefuls at a time, start adding the stock, ensuring that the rice is always covered by a couple of centimetres of liquid.

Cook the risotto like this for 10 minutes, stirring as you go, then add the chopped porcini mushrooms. Cook for a further 8 minutes, then add the parmesan, 50g (11⁄2oz) of the butter and all the mascarpone.

Stir vigorously until the risotto is emulsified, then check the seasoning and the texture of the rice; it should have a nice bite. Turn off the heat, place a lid on the pan and leave the risotto to rest for 2 minutes.
In a small saucepan, melt the remaining 25g (1oz) of butter and add the garlic. Cook for 30 seconds, then add the spinach. Mix well and leave to one side.
Serve the risotto in warmed bowls with a spoonful of the chopped garlicky spinach on top.

stepsZh: Drain the porcini mushrooms, reserving the soaking liquid, and chop them finely.

Heat 2 tablespoons of the olive oil in a large saucepan over a low heat. Once hot, add the onion, leek, celery, carrots, porcini mushrooms and their soaking liquid, and salt. Cook for 20 minutes, until all the vegetables are soft.
Then, add the courgettes (zucchini), increase the heat to medium, and cook for 15 minutes, making sure the courgettes have a little colour and are beginning to soften.
Add the cannellini beans, parsley and boiling water, then bring the minestrone to a simmer. Cook over a low heat for 20 minutes, until everything is melded and soft.
Meanwhile, preheat the oven to 200°C/180°C fan/400°F/Gas 6.
Toss the torn ciabatta pieces in the remaining tablespoon of olive oil and bake in the oven for 5 minutes, until they are crispy.
Stir the crispy ciabatta into the soup and cook gently for a further 10 minutes, so the bread breaks down and thickens the minestrone – it should be very thick.
Check the seasoning and serve with a drizzle more extra-virgin olive oil and some grated parmesan.

recipes.detailsZh: Pork shoulder cooked in milk以2kg (4lb 8oz) pork shoulder, cut in half、75g (21⁄2oz) unsalted butter、1 litre (35fl oz) whole milk, warmed to just below boiling、pared zest and juice of 1 lemon为主要材料，偏家常做法，步骤完整，更适合作为午晚餐主菜或搭配主食。

materialsEn: 1 litre (35fl oz) whole milk, warmed to just below boiling
pared zest and juice of 1 lemon
sea salt and freshly ground black pepper
stepsZh: Preheat the oven to 180°C/160°C fan/350°F/Gas 4.
Season the pork shoulder pieces with plenty of salt and pepper. Set a large, heavy-based saucepan or skillet over a medium–high heat, then add the butter.

When the butter starts to foam, add the seasoned pork shoulder and brown the pieces all over (this will make all the difference to the flavour of the final dish). Remove the pork from the pan and place it to one side.
Pour the browned butter and pork fat into a container to discard (do not pour it down the drain, otherwise you will block your sink).
Put the pan back over a low heat and add the hot milk. Bring the milk to a simmer, then add the lemon zest and juice, the garlic cloves and the chopped sage leaves.
Add the browned pork shoulder pieces back to the pan, then take the pan off the heat and cover it tightly with foil.
Place the pork in the hot oven for 21⁄2 hours, then remove the foil and return the pork to the oven for a further 20 minutes, until lightly browned on top.
Remove the pan from the oven and leave the pork to cool for 10 minutes, then transfer the shoulder pieces to a plate and keep them warm in the turned-off oven.
There should be some nice chunky pieces of curdled milk left in the pan – if you feel there isn't enough liquid, add another 150ml (5fl oz) of hot milk.
Add the cream and set the mixture over a low heat, leaving it to bubble and reduce by half for about 5 minutes.
Slice the rested pork into 2cm (3⁄4in) pieces and place these back into the sauce in the pan. Serve immediately with a big bowl of garlicky braised greens.

recipes.detailsZh: Potato and parmesan croquettes以800g (1lb 12oz) Désirée or Cyprus potatoes, peeled and cut into 2cm (3⁄4in) cubes、50ml (13⁄4fl oz) double (heavy) cream、75g (21⁄2oz) butter、1 garlic clove, crushed to a paste with a little sea salt为主要材料，偏家常做法，步骤完整，更适合作为午晚餐主菜或搭配主食。

materialsZh: 800g (1lb 12oz) Désirée or Cyprus potatoes, peeled and cut into 2cm (3⁄4in) cubes
1 garlic clove, crushed to a paste with a little sea salt
2 eggs, each beaten in a separate bowl
sea salt and freshly ground black pepper
materialsEn: 800g (1lb 12oz) Désirée or Cyprus potatoes, peeled and cut into 2cm (3⁄4in) cubes
1 garlic clove, crushed to a paste with a little sea salt
2 eggs, each beaten in a separate bowl
sea salt and freshly ground black pepper
stepsZh: Tip the potatoes into a large saucepan with 1 teaspoon of sea salt and cover them with cold water. Place the pan over a medium heat and cook the potatoes for about 25 minutes, or until a knife goes through them easily.
Drain and allow them to steam dry in the colander for at least 2 minutes, then tip the potatoes into a bowl and bash them with a whisk until the potato has become finely mashed. Set aside.
Heat the cream in a small saucepan with the butter and garlic. Bring the cream to a simmer, then pour this over the mashed potato. Beat with the whisk until the mash is very smooth and creamy.
Add the parmesan and one of the beaten eggs and mix to combine, then stir through the chopped parsley and check the seasoning. Leave to cool to room temperature.

Once cool, take a tablespoonful of the mixture and shape it into a golf-ball-sized ball, then gently push the potato down to shape it into a round but flat puck. Repeat until you have used up the mixture.
Place the potato pucks on a tray and chill them in the fridge for 20 minutes.

Place the breadcrumbs on a large plate, the flour on another and the remaining beaten egg in a shallow bowl. Take a potato puck and first coat it in the flour, then the beaten egg, and finally the breadcrumbs.
Place the coated puck back on the tray and repeat with the remainder.

Heat the sunflower oil in a medium saucepan over a medium heat until the oil is shiny but not smoking. Carefully lower three breaded pucks into the hot oil and cook them for about 5 minutes, until they are a nice, golden brown.

Use a slotted spoon to remove them from the oil and place them on a tray lined with kitchen paper to absorb any excess oil. Repeat this process, frying 3 croquettes at a time, until you have cooked them all.
Keep them warm in a low oven and serve them with lemon wedges and a little sea salt for sprinkling over.

recipes.detailsZh: Rabbit with honey, prunes and mustard以2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil、4 rabbit legs, seasoned with salt and pepper、75g (21⁄2oz) pancetta、2 celery stalks, finely chopped为主要材料，偏家常做法，步骤完整，更适合作为午晚餐主菜或搭配主食。
recipes.detailsEn: Rabbit with honey, prunes and mustard以2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil、4 rabbit legs, seasoned with salt and pepper、75g (21⁄2oz) pancetta、2 celery stalks, finely chopped为主要材料，偏家常做法，步骤完整，更适合作为午晚餐主菜或搭配主食。
materialsZh: 4 rabbit legs, seasoned with salt and pepper
sea salt and freshly ground black pepper
materialsEn: 4 rabbit legs, seasoned with salt and pepper
sea salt and freshly ground black pepper
stepsZh: Preheat the oven to 200°C/180°C fan/400°F/Gas 6.

Heat 1 tablespoon of the olive oil in a large, heavy-based casserole pan over a medium heat, then add the rabbit legs and sear them for about 5 minutes, turning, until a nice golden brown all over. Set the legs aside on a plate.

Add the pancetta, celery, onion and rosemary to the hot casserole pan and fry them over a medium heat for 5 minutes so the pancetta gets some colour, and the celery and onions are soft. Add the white wine and bring the liquid to a simmer.

Carefully place the browned rabbit legs back into the casserole, then scatter over the prunes and add the honey and hot water. Cover the casserole tightly with foil so there are no gaps and place the rabbit in the oven for 45 minutes.
Leave the rabbit to rest in the casserole pan for 10 minutes, then carefully remove the rabbit legs to a plate, cover the plate tightly with foil, to keep the moisture in, and keep warm.
Place the casserole over a medium heat and bring the liquid to a simmer. Simmer until the liquid has reduced by half, then add the cream and cook for a further 5 minutes over a low heat.
Stir through the parsley and check the seasoning, adjusting with salt and pepper as necessary. Return the cooked rabbit legs to the casserole pan and spoon over the creamy sauce.
I like to serve this with mashed celeriac and some braised greens.

recipes.titleEn: Rabbit with pine nuts and olives

recipes.subtitleEn: 一锅可做 · 4 rabbit legs, seasoned with salt and pepper · 50g (13⁄4oz) plain (all-purpose) flour, for dusting

materialsZh: 4 rabbit legs, seasoned with salt and pepper
sea salt and freshly ground black pepper
1 garlic clove, crushed to a paste with a little sea salt
materialsEn: 4 rabbit legs, seasoned with salt and pepper
sea salt and freshly ground black pepper
1 garlic clove, crushed to a paste with a little sea salt
stepsZh: First, make the gremolata. Mix together all the gremolata ingredients in a bowl, cover the bowl and refrigerate until you’re ready to serve.
Preheat the oven to 180°C/160°C fan/350°F/Gas 4.
Toss the seasoned rabbit legs in a bowl with the flour, shaking off any excess.

Heat the oil in large casserole pan over a medium heat. When hot, add the rabbit legs and sear for about 5 minutes, turning, until evenly coloured on all sides. Remove the legs from the pan and set them aside on a plate.
Add the onion, celery, thyme leaves, olives, pine nuts and garlic to the pan and cook gently for 5 minutes, until the onion has softened.
Add the tomato pulp to the pan and leave it to reduce for 2 minutes, then add the fennel, white wine and hot water. Bring the liquid to a simmer, then return the rabbit legs to the pan.
Spoon the liquid over the rabbit so it has some of the vegetables, olives and pine nuts on top. Cover the casserole with foil and/or a tight-fitting lid and transfer it to the oven for 1 hour.

Remove the pan from the oven and take off the foil or lid. Rest the casserole for 5 minutes, then remove the rabbit legs with a slotted spoon and transfer them to a large plate. Cover the plate with foil and keep warm to one side.
Place the pan back over a medium–high heat and bring the liquid to a simmer. Reduce until it’s thick enough to coat the back of a spoon.
Place the rabbit legs on to a warm serving dish and pour the reduced cooking liquid over the top. Finish with a sprinkle of gremolata. Serve with some creamy mashed potatoes and braised greens.

recipes.subtitleZh: 一锅可做 · 2 egg whites · 300g (101⁄2oz) icing (confectioner’s) sugar, sifted
recipes.subtitleEn: 一锅可做 · 2 egg whites · 300g (101⁄2oz) icing (confectioner’s) sugar, sifted
recipes.detailsZh: Ricciarelli以2 egg whites、300g (101⁄2oz) icing (confectioner’s) sugar, sifted、250g (9oz) ground almonds、75g (21⁄2oz) toasted pine nuts为主要材料，偏家常做法，步骤完整，更适合作为午晚餐主菜或搭配主食。
recipes.detailsEn: Ricciarelli以2 egg whites、300g (101⁄2oz) icing (confectioner’s) sugar, sifted、250g (9oz) ground almonds、75g (21⁄2oz) toasted pine nuts为主要材料，偏家常做法，步骤完整，更适合作为午晚餐主菜或搭配主食。
stepsZh: Preheat the oven to 200°C/180°C fan/400°F/Gas 6. Line a large baking sheet with baking paper.
In a very clean mixing bowl, use a hand-held electric whisk to whisk the egg whites to stiff peaks.
Place 150g (51⁄2oz) of the icing (confectioner’s) sugar in a separate large mixing bowl, along with all the other ingredients, and mix thoroughly.
With a large metal spoon, add a spoonful of the egg whites to the other ingredients, then gently fold them together to loosen.
Add the remaining egg whites and gently fold everything together until no streaks remain – the mixture will feel sticky.
Evenly dust the remaining icing sugar over a tray. Scoop a generous teaspoonful of the mixture, then roll it between your hands to a form ball.
Place the ball on the dusted tray and repeat until the mixture is all used up (you should have about 12 balls).

Gently roll all the balls around in the icing sugar until they are completely coated (the icing sugar will dry the outer part of the ricciarelli so they become cracked on top but remain chewy in the middle).
Transfer the balls to the lined baking sheet, spacing them evenly apart. Push down on each ball with the palm of your hand to create little puck shapes.
Bake the ricciarelli for 20 minutes, until lightly golden. Remove them from the oven and carefully transfer them to a wire rack to cool completely.
They are delicious as an after-dinner petit four or served with a coffee for an afternoon pick-me-up.

recipes.titleZh: Roast duck with honey and citrus
recipes.titleEn: Roast duck with honey and citrus
recipes.subtitleZh: 一锅可做 · 1 Gressingham duck (about 2kg/4lb 8oz), with giblets · 1 leek, roughly chopped
recipes.subtitleEn: 一锅可做 · 1 Gressingham duck (about 2kg/4lb 8oz), with giblets · 1 leek, roughly chopped
recipes.detailsZh: Roast duck with honey and citrus以1 Gressingham duck (about 2kg/4lb 8oz), with giblets、1 leek, roughly chopped、1 carrot, peeled and roughly chopped、1 celery stalk, roughly chopped为主要材料，偏家常做法，步骤完整，更适合作为午晚餐主菜或搭配主食。
recipes.detailsEn: Roast duck with honey and citrus以1 Gressingham duck (about 2kg/4lb 8oz), with giblets、1 leek, roughly chopped、1 carrot, peeled and roughly chopped、1 celery stalk, roughly chopped为主要材料，偏家常做法，步骤完整，更适合作为午晚餐主菜或搭配主食。
stepsZh: Preheat the oven to 200°C/180°C fan/400°F/Gas 6.

Remove the giblets from the duck and place them in a baking tray with the leek, carrot, celery and parsley stalks. Transfer the tray to the bottom of the oven and cook the vegetables and giblets for 30 minutes.

Pour off any excess fat from the pan, then place the giblets and vegetables in a large saucepan with 1 litre (35fl oz) of cold water. Bring to a boil over a high heat and allow to reduce by half (about 20 minutes). Leave to one side.
Mix together the orange, lemon and thyme and use the mixture to stuff the cavity of the duck. Place a wire rack into your roasting tin and place the stuffed duck in the middle of the rack.
Rub a sheet of foil with olive oil on the dull side and use this to to cover the duck so that there are no gaps (the oil stops the duck skin sticking to the foil).
Roast the duck for 45 minutes, then remove the foil and pour all the juices into a jug (there will be a lot of duck fat in this juice).

Run a serrated knife all over the duck to release the fat deposits that are on the surface. Dab the duck with some kitchen paper to dry the surface, then use a pastry brush to brush 75g (21⁄2oz) of the honey all over the duck.
Return the duck to the oven, uncovered, for 1 hour, until lightly golden.

While the duck is roasting, make a sauce. Skim off the fat from the duck cooking liquid. Melt the butter in a small saucepan and add the shallots. Fry gently for 5 minutes, until softened, then add the port.
Bring to a simmer and reduce the liquid by half, then add the remaining honey. Stir in the skimmed duck juice and the stock from the roasted giblets.
Cook over a medium heat, until the liquid has reduced to about 150ml (5fl oz), then skim off any excess fat and keep the sauce warm on one side.
Once the duck is ready, remove it from the oven, then carve off the legs and breasts, halving the breasts. Place them on a nice serving dish then pour over half the sauce.
Serve the remaining sauce in a small jug on the side for your guests to pour over. I love this dish served with buttered pearl barley and Savoy cabbage.

recipes.subtitleZh: 一锅可做 · 2kg (4lb 8oz) very fresh mussels in their shells · 4 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil
recipes.subtitleEn: 一锅可做 · 2kg (4lb 8oz) very fresh mussels in their shells · 4 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil
recipes.detailsZh: Saffron and seafood linguine以2kg (4lb 8oz) very fresh mussels in their shells、4 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil、2 garlic cloves, finely sliced、150ml (5fl oz) dry white wine为主要材料，偏家常做法，步骤完整，更适合作为午晚餐主菜或搭配主食。
recipes.detailsEn: Saffron and seafood linguine以2kg (4lb 8oz) very fresh mussels in their shells、4 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil、2 garlic cloves, finely sliced、150ml (5fl oz) dry white wine为主要材料，偏家常做法，步骤完整，更适合作为午晚餐主菜或搭配主食。
materialsZh: 2kg (4lb 8oz) very fresh mussels in their shells
sea salt and freshly ground black pepper
Clean the mussels thoroughly and remove the beards.
materialsEn: 2kg (4lb 8oz) very fresh mussels in their shells
sea salt and freshly ground black pepper
Clean the mussels thoroughly and remove the beards.
stepsZh: Heat 2 tablespoons of the olive oil in a large saucepan over a medium heat. When hot, add the mussels and the garlic, then place the lid on the pan and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the white wine and thyme, then leave the mussels to cook for a further 4 minutes, until they have cooked through (discard any that don’t open).
Take off the lid and pour the mussels into a colander set over a large bowl to collect the cooking juices.
Once the mussels have cooled a little, select 20 of the best for garnish and keep them to one side. Remove the meat from the rest of the mussels and discard the shells. Keep the meat to one side.

Pass the cooking juices through a fine sieve or (better still) a coffee filter, to remove any small pieces of grit, then pour it into a large non-stick frying pan. Add the saffron and place the pan over a medium heat.
Simmer the juices for about 3 minutes to reduce them by half, then add the cream. Bring the sauce back to a simmer, season with black pepper and turn off the heat.
Add the remaining olive oil to a small saucepan over a medium heat. When hot, add the breadcrumbs and cook them for a couple of minutes, stirring from time to time, until they are light golden brown.
Drain the pan into a fine sieve to get rid of the oil, then tip the drained breadcrumbs on to a plate lined with kitchen paper. Season with salt and set aside.
Bring a large pan of salted water to a boil over a high heat. Add the linguine and cook for 3 minutes less than the packet suggests, until very al dente.
Meanwhile, place the sauce back over a low heat. When the pasta is ready, use a pair of tongs to transfer the linguine to the pan with the sauce.
Add 1 ladleful of the pasta cooking water and then add the mussel meat (along with any juice from the plate) and cook the pasta in the pan for another 2 minutes.
Add the 20 mussels that you kept aside, along with the parsley, then toss until everything is nicely emulsified, adding more pasta water if needed.
Serve immediately in warmed pasta bowls with a generous amount of crispy breadcrumbs sprinkled on top.

recipes.subtitleZh: 一锅可做 · 1kg (2lb 4oz) salsify, washed and peeled · juice of 1 lemon
recipes.subtitleEn: 一锅可做 · 1kg (2lb 4oz) salsify, washed and peeled · juice of 1 lemon
recipes.detailsZh: Salsify al forno以1kg (2lb 4oz) salsify, washed and peeled、juice of 1 lemon、150ml (5fl oz) double (heavy) cream、150ml (5fl oz) whole milk为主要材料，偏家常做法，步骤完整，更适合作为午晚餐主菜或搭配主食。
recipes.detailsEn: Salsify al forno以1kg (2lb 4oz) salsify, washed and peeled、juice of 1 lemon、150ml (5fl oz) double (heavy) cream、150ml (5fl oz) whole milk为主要材料，偏家常做法，步骤完整，更适合作为午晚餐主菜或搭配主食。
materialsZh: 1 garlic clove, crushed to a paste with a little sea salt
summer or autumn black truffle, to serve
materialsEn: 1 garlic clove, crushed to a paste with a little sea salt
summer or autumn black truffle, to serve
stepsZh: Preheat the oven to 200°C/180°C fan/400°F/Gas 6.
Slice the salsify at an angle into 5cm (2in) pieces. Place the pieces in a bowl of cold water, stir through the lemon juice and leave the pieces for 10 minutes.
It’s important the salsify absorbs the lemon juice, as it will prevent it from discolouring when cooked.

Meanwhile, bring a saucepan of salted water to a boil. When the salsify is ready, add it to the water and cook it for 15 minutes, or until you can just put a sharp knife through the middle of each piece.
Drain the salsify in a colander and leave it to steam dry for 5 minutes.

Pour the cream and milk into a small saucepan and set the pan over a low heat. When the cream mixture reaches a simmer, add the garlic and turn off the heat. Set the mixture aside for a couple of minutes, then stir in the parmesan.

Grease a baking dish with the olive oil, then lay the salsify pieces evenly over the base of the dish. Pour over the cream and parmesan mixture and then bake the salsify al forno for 20 minutes, until golden and bubbling.
To serve, shave over some black truffle.

recipes.titleZh: Slow-braised duck legs with wet polenta
recipes.titleEn: Slow-braised duck legs with wet polenta
recipes.subtitleZh: 一锅可做 · 4 duck legs · 100g (31⁄2oz) pancetta
recipes.subtitleEn: 一锅可做 · 4 duck legs · 100g (31⁄2oz) pancetta
recipes.detailsZh: Slow-braised duck legs with wet polenta以4 duck legs、100g (31⁄2oz) pancetta、1 carrot, peeled and finely chopped、2 celery stalks, finely chopped为主要材料，偏家常做法，步骤完整，更适合作为午晚餐主菜或搭配主食。

materialsZh: 20g (3⁄4oz) dried porcini mushrooms, just covered in boiling water and left to soak
sea salt and freshly ground black pepper
1 garlic clove, crushed to a paste with a little sea salt
materialsEn: 20g (3⁄4oz) dried porcini mushrooms, just covered in boiling water and left to soak
sea salt and freshly ground black pepper
1 garlic clove, crushed to a paste with a little sea salt
stepsZh: Preheat the oven to 180°C/160°C fan/350°F/Gas 4.

Heat a large, heavy-based casserole pan over a medium heat. Add the duck legs, skin-side down, and reduce the heat so that the fat on the outside of each leg starts to melt and take on a little colour.
Sear on either side for 4 minutes, until they are lightly coloured all over. Remove the legs from the pan and set aside, leaving the fat in the the pan.
Add the pancetta, carrot, celery, thyme and onion to the fat in the pan and cook gently for 5 minutes, until the onion is soft but not coloured.
Roughly chop the soaked porcini and add them to the pan, then strain in the soaking liquid through a coffee filter or a sieve lined with kitchen paper.
Add the red wine and port, simmer for 2–3 minutes to evaporate the alcohol, then stir in the passata and hot water.
Place the lid on the casserole or cover it tightly with foil and bake in the oven for 90 minutes, until the legs are cooked through and the meat is very tender.
Remove the pan from the oven and leave to cool for 15 minutes. Meanwhile, reduce the oven to 140°C/120°C fan/275°F/Gas 1.
With a slotted spoon, take out the cooked duck legs and set them aside on a plate. With a pair of disposable gloves, carefully pull off all the duck fat and pick off the duck meat from the bones.
When you have all the meat separated from the bones and the duck fat, place the meat back into the casserole. Discard the bones and fat.
Mix the duck meat in with all the cooking liquid and vegetables then taste and season. Replace the lid or foil and return the casserole to the oven while you make the polenta and gremolata.
For the polenta, pour 400ml (14fl oz) of water into a medium saucepan and place it over a high heat. Bring it to a boil and add a big pinch of salt.

Add the red wine and port, simmer for 2–3 minutes to evaporate the alcohol, then stir in the passata and hot water.

recipes.detailsZh: Stuffed globe artichokes以8 globe artichokes、small bunch of flat-leaf parsley、For the stuffing、100g (31⁄2oz) dried breadcrumbs为主要材料，偏家常做法，步骤完整，更适合作为午晚餐主菜或搭配主食。

materialsZh: 1 garlic clove, crushed to a paste with a little sea salt
generous pinch each of sea salt and freshly ground black pepper
materialsEn: 1 garlic clove, crushed to a paste with a little sea salt
generous pinch each of sea salt and freshly ground black pepper
stepsZh: Take each artichoke and peel off the outer leaves until you get to the lighter-coloured leaves. Using a speedy peeler, peel the outer green part of the stems and heart.
Then cut the top off the artichoke with a sharp kitchen knife or bread knife, to expose the heart of the artichoke. Using a teaspoon or melon baller, scoop out the thistly choke.
If there is very little thistly choke, then the artichoke is young and will be very tender – this is good. The older ones with lots of choke are fine but may be slightly more arduous to prepare.

Once you have prepared the artichokes, place them in a bowl of water. Lightly bash the parsley, then add this to the bowl too – this will prevent the artichokes oxidizing, which makes them change colour and taste bitter.
You can use lemon instead of parsley, but I find lemon can overpower the flavour of the artichoke.
Leave the artichokes in the water with the parsley for 10 minutes, then take them out and leave them to one side ready to be stuffed, ensuring there is no residual water left inside the artichoke.
Preheat the oven to 200°C/180°C fan /400°F/Gas 6.

To make the stuffing add all the stuffing ingredients, except the wine, to a bowl and mix well. Evenly divide the stuffing between the artichokes, then place them on their sides in a lightly oiled baking dish.
Add the wine and 75ml (21⁄4fl oz) of water to the dish and cover it tightly with foil.
Bake the stuffed artichokes for 30 minutes, then remove the foil and bake them for a further 10 minutes.
Leave the artichokes to cool for 5 minutes, then serve them on their own, or with some sliced prosciutto di Parma and asiago cheese as an antipasto.

recipes.subtitleEn: 一锅可做 · 75g (21⁄2oz) butter · 100g (31⁄2oz) muscovado sugar
recipes.detailsZh: Sweet green tomato tart以75g (21⁄2oz) butter、100g (31⁄2oz) muscovado sugar、1 vanilla pod, split lengthways and seeds scraped out and reserved、6 large green tomatoes, halved through the middle为主要材料，偏家常做法，步骤完整，更适合作为午晚餐主菜或搭配主食。
recipes.detailsEn: Sweet green tomato tart以75g (21⁄2oz) butter、100g (31⁄2oz) muscovado sugar、1 vanilla pod, split lengthways and seeds scraped out and reserved、6 large green tomatoes, halved through the middle为主要材料，偏家常做法，步骤完整，更适合作为午晚餐主菜或搭配主食。
materialsZh: 1 vanilla pod, split lengthways and seeds scraped out and reserved
6 large green tomatoes, halved through the middle
materialsEn: 1 vanilla pod, split lengthways and seeds scraped out and reserved
6 large green tomatoes, halved through the middle
stepsZh: Preheat the oven to 200°C/180°C fan/400°F/Gas 6.

Melt the butter in a small non-stick, ovenproof frying pan and add the muscovado sugar, the vanilla pod and the vanilla seeds and cook for 5 minutes, stirring with a wooden spoon, until the sugar and butter have melted into a syrup.
Place the tomatoes cut-side down into the hot syrup and cook for 5 minutes over a low heat.
Meanwhile, cut the puff pastry sheet into a circle to match the diameter of the frying pan, then transfer it to a piece of baking paper and chill it in the fridge for 10 minutes.

Take the tomato pan off the heat, then carefully top it with the puff pastry, pushing the edges down inside the edges of the pan to form a seal. Bake the tart in the oven for 25 minutes, until the pastry is golden.
Remove the frying pan from the oven and place it on a wire cooling rack. Leave the tart to rest and cool in the pan for at least 40 minutes.
Once the tart has cooled, return the frying pan to a low heat for a couple of minutes, to allow to sugars to melt a little. Then, take a large, flat plate and place it on top of the frying pan.
Place your palm in the middle of the plate and the other hand on the handle of the frying pan, then flip everything so that you invert the tart on to the plate.

Lift away the frying pan and the sweet tomato tart should be in the middle of the plate in one piece. Serve immediately with a dusting of icing (confectioner’s) sugar and a spoonful of cold crème fraîche.

materialsZh: sea salt and freshly ground black pepper
materialsEn: sea salt and freshly ground black pepper
stepsZh: Cut the stems off the Swiss chard and cut them into 1cm (1⁄2in) slices. Slice the leaves into 2cm (3⁄4in) pieces.
Bring a large saucepan of salted water to a boil and add the chard stems. Cook for 2 minutes, then add the leaves and cook for a further 2 minutes.
Drain the blanched chard leaves and stems in a colander and press down with a wooden spoon to extract any excess water. Set aside.
Heat the oil in a large non-stick frying pan over a medium heat. Add the onions, reduce the heat to low, and cook for 10 minutes, until they are soft but not coloured.
Add the chard and cook for about 5 minutes, until there is no excess water. Take the pan off the heat and leave to cool a little. Season with salt and pepper.
Preheat the oven to 200°C/180°C fan/400°F/Gas 6.
Place the sheet of puff pastry on to a baking sheet.
Crack 1 egg into a cup, add the milk and beat together lightly with a fork. Using a pastry brush, paint the top of the pastry so that it is completely coated in the egg mixture.
Bake the pastry in the oven for 20 minutes, until risen. Transfer to a wire cooling rack on the baking sheet to cool for 15 mintues. Leave the oven on.
Beat the remaining eggs in a large bowl and add the crème fraîche, chard and onions, and thyme. Mix everything together well and check the seasoning.
When the pastry has cooled, gently push down the puffed surface so that it is flat again, then spoon on the mixture, leaving a 1cm (1⁄2in) gap around the edge.
Scatter the chopped olives evenly over the filling, then top with the sliced garlic and scamorza.

Bake the tart for 20 minutes, until the scamorza has melted and has a little colour on top. Leave the tart to cool for a few minutes, then slice and serve as a light lunch, or as a nibble with drinks.

recipes.subtitleEn: 一锅可做 · 300g (101⁄2oz) ripe cherry tomatoes · 3 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil
recipes.detailsZh: Tomato and sardine crostata以300g (101⁄2oz) ripe cherry tomatoes、3 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil、1 garlic clove, finely sliced、300g (101⁄2oz) tomato passata为主要材料，偏家常做法，步骤完整，更适合作为午晚餐主菜或搭配主食。
recipes.detailsEn: Tomato and sardine crostata以300g (101⁄2oz) ripe cherry tomatoes、3 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil、1 garlic clove, finely sliced、300g (101⁄2oz) tomato passata为主要材料，偏家常做法，步骤完整，更适合作为午晚餐主菜或搭配主食。
materialsZh: sea salt and freshly ground black pepper
materialsEn: sea salt and freshly ground black pepper
stepsZh: Preheat the oven to 200°C/180°C fan/400°F/Gas 4.
Place the cherry tomatoes in a small saucepan or bowl. Using a stick blender, blitz them to a smooth pulp.

Heat 1 tablespoon of the olive oil in a large non-stick frying pan over a medium heat and add the garlic. Cook the garlic for 30 seconds, then add the blitzed cherry tomatoes. Cook for a further 2 minutes, then add the tomato passata.
Reduce the heat to low and simmer for about 15 minutes, until the tomato sauce has reduced by half and is thick and syrupy. Season with salt and pepper and keep to one side.
Lightly flour a baking sheet. Remove the puff pastry from the packaging and cut it into a circle that is roughly 25cm (10in) in diameter, then transfer it to the baking sheet.

Brush the pastry all over with the beaten egg, then bake it in the oven ( just as it is, without any filling) for 15 minutes. The puff pastry will rise considerably, which is what we want as it needs to cook all the way through.
Place the baking sheet on a wire cooling rack after you have removed it from the oven and leave it to cool to room temperature.
When the pastry has cooled, gently push down the puffed surface so that it is flat again, then spoon on the tomato sauce.
Toss the sardine fillets in a bowl with 1 tablespoon of the remaining olive oil, the chopped parsley, the dried oregano, and some salt and pepper.
Carefully place the sardine fillets skin side up on top of the tomato sauce like a clock face. Sprinkle over the capers, then place the tart back in the oven for a further 20 minutes.
Remove the tart from the oven and leave it to cool, then serve with a dressed green salad.
stepsEn: Preheat the oven to 200°C/180°C fan/400°F/Gas 4.
Place the cherry tomatoes in a small saucepan or bowl. Using a stick blender, blitz them to a smooth pulp.

Heat 1 tablespoon of the olive oil in a large non-stick frying pan over a medium heat and add the garlic. Cook the garlic for 30 seconds, then add the blitzed cherry tomatoes. Cook for a further 2 minutes, then add the tomato passata.
Reduce the heat to low and simmer for about 15 minutes, until the tomato sauce has reduced by half and is thick and syrupy. Season with salt and pepper and keep to one side.
Lightly flour a baking sheet. Remove the puff pastry from the packaging and cut it into a circle that is roughly 25cm (10in) in diameter, then transfer it to the baking sheet.

Brush the pastry all over with the beaten egg, then bake it in the oven ( just as it is, without any filling) for 15 minutes. The puff pastry will rise considerably, which is what we want as it needs to cook all the way through.
Place the baking sheet on a wire cooling rack after you have removed it from the oven and leave it to cool to room temperature.
When the pastry has cooled, gently push down the puffed surface so that it is flat again, then spoon on the tomato sauce.
Toss the sardine fillets in a bowl with 1 tablespoon of the remaining olive oil, the chopped parsley, the dried oregano, and some salt and pepper.
Carefully place the sardine fillets skin side up on top of the tomato sauce like a clock face. Sprinkle over the capers, then place the tart back in the oven for a further 20 minutes.
Remove the tart from the oven and leave it to cool, then serve with a dressed green salad.
notesZh: Serves 6 as a starter
notesEn: Serves 6 as a starter

materialsZh: 450g (1lb) tipo OO flour, plus extra for dusting
materialsEn: 450g (1lb) tipo OO flour, plus extra for dusting
stepsZh: First, make the pastry. Mix the flour and the icing (confectioner’s) sugar together in a large mixing bowl. Add the lemon zest and butter.

Run your hands under the cold tap for a minute to make sure they are really cold, then dry them and, using your fingertips, work the flour, sugar, zest and butter together until the mixture resembles breadcrumbs.
Add the beaten egg yolks and mix together so the yolks are even distributed. If the pastry feels dry, add 1 teaspoon of water and form the pastry into a round, smooth ball.
Using the palm of your hand, press the pastry into a 2cm (3⁄4in)-thick disc, wrap it in cling film (plastic wrap) and refrigerate it for 20 minutes.

Lightly flour your work surface. Divide the chilled pastry in half, wrap one half again and set it aside. Roll out the first half to a disc a few inches larger in diameter than a 28cm (11in) fluted tart tin.
Transfer the pastry to the tart tin, pressing it into the base and sides, and leaving any overhang.
Unwrap the remaining half of the dough and roll this out to a disc very slightly larger than the tart tin. This will be the lid.
Transfer the lid to a sheet of baking paper and then place this and the tart case in the fridge while you make the filling.
Preheat the oven to 180°C/160°C fan/350°F/Gas 4.
Pour the milk into a large saucepan and place it over a low–medium heat. Add the pared lemon zest and bring the milk to a gentle simmer.
Meanwhile, in a large bowl, whisk the egg yolks with the sugar until they turn a pale, creamy colour. Whisk in the cornflour (corn starch) and vanilla then set aside.
Scoop out the lemon zest strips from the milk using a slotted spoon and then slowly whisk the warm, infused milk into the egg and sugar mixture.

Once you have added all the milk, pour the contents of the bowl back into the saucepan and return the pan to a low heat. Cook the custard very gently for 10–12 minutes, until it is smooth and thick enough to coat the back of a spoon.
Pour the custard into a shallow dish to cool completely.

Spoon the thick, cooled custard into the chilled tart case in an even layer. Top with the pastry lid and press the pastry edges together to encase the custard and seal it in completely. Trim away any overhang.
Whisk together the egg and milk for the egg wash, then brush this over the pastry lid, ensuring the top of the torta is completely coated. Scatter over the pine nuts.

Bake the torta for 60 minutes, until the pastry is golden and crisp. Remove the torta from the oven and set it on a wire rack to cool completely in the tin. Once cool, dust it generously with a coating of icing (confectioner’s) sugar.
Serve in slices with a spoonful of crema di mascarpone.

recipes.detailsZh: Torta pastiera以For the pastry、250g (9oz) tipo OO flour、100g (31⁄2oz) unsalted butter、75g (21⁄2oz) icing (confectioner’s) sugar, plus extra for dusting为主要材料，偏家常做法，步骤完整，更适合作为午晚餐主菜或搭配主食。
recipes.detailsEn: Torta pastiera以For the pastry、250g (9oz) tipo OO flour、100g (31⁄2oz) unsalted butter、75g (21⁄2oz) icing (confectioner’s) sugar, plus extra for dusting为主要材料，偏家常做法，步骤完整，更适合作为午晚餐主菜或搭配主食。
materialsZh: 75g (21⁄2oz) icing (confectioner’s) sugar, plus extra for dusting
150g (51⁄2oz) grano cotto (or, pre-boil some risotto rice in water for 15 minutes until al dente; drain and cool)
75g (21⁄2oz) candied orange and lemon peel, chopped
materialsEn: 75g (21⁄2oz) icing (confectioner’s) sugar, plus extra for dusting
150g (51⁄2oz) grano cotto (or, pre-boil some risotto rice in water for 15 minutes until al dente; drain and cool)
75g (21⁄2oz) candied orange and lemon peel, chopped
stepsZh: First make the pastry. Sift the flour into a large bowl, and add the butter, icing (confectioner’s) sugar and salt.
Run your hands under the cold tap for a minute to make sure they are really cold, then dry them and, using your fingertips, work everything together until the mixture is almost like breadcrumbs.

Add the beaten egg, along with the milk, honey and lemon and orange zests. Mix well to combine, bringing the dough together into a smooth ball. Flatten the ball into a disc about 2cm (3⁄4in) thick with the palm of your hand.
Wrap the disc in cling film (plastic wrap) and leave it in the fridge to rest for 15 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 170°C/150°C fan/325°F/Gas 3.
Meanwhile, make the filling. Place the rice in a large saucepan with the milk and lemon zest. Place the pan over a medium heat and bring the mixture to a simmer.
Simmer for 15 minutes, then pour the mixture out over a large, clean baking tray to cool down.
In a large bowl, ideally with an electric hand whisk, whisk the whole eggs and egg yolks with the caster (superfine) sugar until pale in colour.
In another bowl, again using the electric hand whisk if you have one, whisk the ricotta for about 4 minutes so it is light and fluffy. Fold the ricotta into the beaten eggs.

Add the cold cooked rice mixture, candied orange and lemon peel, vanilla seeds and orange blossom water (if using). Gently fold everything together so all the ingredients are well combined. Leave to one side.
Dust your work surface with icing (confectioner’s) sugar and remove the pastry from the fridge.
Roll out the pastry to a disc about 5mm (1⁄4in) thick, then transfer the disc to a loose-bottomed cake tin and press the pastry into the tin, leaving an overhang.

Using a sharp knife, cut off the excess pastry and shape these trimmings into a ball. Roll out the ball of trimmings to a rectangle about 5mm (1⁄4in) thick and, using a pasta ravioli cutter, cut strips from the rectangle of dough.Leave to one side.

Pour the filling mixture into the raw pastry case, then cover it with the strips of pastry and trim any overhang (see photograph). Bake the torta for 80 minutes, until a skewer inserted into the centre comes out clean.

Transfer the torta in the tin to a wire rack and leave it to cool completely. You can eat it on the day you bake it, but Italians tend to eat it at least one day after baking, as the flavour just gets better.
Dust with icing (confectioner’s) sugar before serving.

recipes.detailsZh: Traditional Sicilian cassata以For the pastry、400g (14oz) tipo OO flour, plus extra for dusting、225g (8oz) unsalted butter, cut into 1cm (1⁄2in) cubes and chilled、140g (11⁄2oz) caster (superfine) sugar为主要材料，偏家常做法，步骤完整，更适合作为午晚餐主菜或搭配主食。

materialsZh: 400g (14oz) tipo OO flour, plus extra for dusting
225g (8oz) unsalted butter, cut into 1cm (1⁄2in) cubes and chilled
200g (7oz) icing (confectioner’s) sugar, sifted, plus extra for dusting
100g (31⁄2oz) finely broken 70% dark (bittersweet) chocolate or 70% dark chocolate drops
materialsEn: 400g (14oz) tipo OO flour, plus extra for dusting

stepsZh: First make the pastry. Sift the flour into a large bowl, and add the butter, sugar, salt and both citrus zests.
Run your hands under the cold tap for a minute to make sure they are really cold, then dry them and, using your fingertips, work everything together until the mixture is almost like breadcrumbs.
Add the egg yolks and mix well to combine, bringing the dough together into a smooth ball. Divide the pastry in half and form each half into a ball.
Flatten each into a disc about 2cm (3⁄4in) thick and wrap them in cling film (plastic wrap). Rest them in the fridge for 40 minutes.

While the pastry is resting, make the filling. In a large bowl, whisk the ricotta with the icing (confectioner’s) sugar until you have a smooth, creamy texture, then fold in the chocolate and candied orange pieces.
Cover the bowl with cling film and refrigerate the filling until you’re ready to use it.
Preheat the oven to 200°C/180°C fan/400°F/Gas 6.
One by one, use a rolling pin to roll out the 2 halves of pastry on a lightly floured work surface until 5mm (1⁄4in) thick.
Place one half of the rolled pastry into a loose-bottomed 24cm (10in) fluted tart tin, to line the base and sides, pressing it gently into the corners to create a neat fit.
Use a fork to prick the base all over, then pour in the ricotta mixture. Carefully place the remaining round of pastry on top, pressing the edges together to seal. Cut off the excess.
Bake the cassata for 50 minutes, until the filling is piping hot and the top is golden. Remove the cassata from the oven and transfer it in the tin to a wire rack to cool for at least 2 hours.
Dust the pie with icing (confectioner’s) sugar and serve it at room temperature as a dessert or with some really good hot coffee for an afternoon treat.

recipes.subtitleEn: 一锅可做 · 500g (1lb 2oz) baby San Marzano or datterini tomatoes · 4 large prawns (shrimp), heads on
recipes.detailsZh: Venetian fish stew以500g (1lb 2oz) baby San Marzano or datterini tomatoes、4 large prawns (shrimp), heads on、3 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil、1 celery stalk, roughly chopped为主要材料，偏家常做法，步骤完整，更适合作为午晚餐主菜或搭配主食。
recipes.detailsEn: Venetian fish stew以500g (1lb 2oz) baby San Marzano or datterini tomatoes、4 large prawns (shrimp), heads on、3 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil、1 celery stalk, roughly chopped为主要材料，偏家常做法，步骤完整，更适合作为午晚餐主菜或搭配主食。
materialsZh: 500g (1lb 2oz) baby San Marzano or datterini tomatoes
1 small fennel bulb, cut into eighths
1 carrot, peeled and cut into 1cm (1⁄2in) pieces
250g (9oz) very fresh mussels in their shells, cleaned and debearded
1 garlic clove, finely chopped, plus extra for the toast
1 small ciabatta loaf, cut into 2cm (3⁄4in) slices
sea salt and freshly ground black pepper
materialsEn: 500g (1lb 2oz) baby San Marzano or datterini tomatoes
1 small fennel bulb, cut into eighths
1 carrot, peeled and cut into 1cm (1⁄2in) pieces
250g (9oz) very fresh mussels in their shells, cleaned and debearded
1 garlic clove, finely chopped, plus extra for the toast
1 small ciabatta loaf, cut into 2cm (3⁄4in) slices
sea salt and freshly ground black pepper
stepsZh: Tip the tomatoes into a small saucepan or bowl. Using a stick blender, blitz them to a smooth pulp. Set them aside.
Peel the prawns (shrimp) and take off the heads. Reserve the flesh to one side and place the heads and shells in a saucepan over a high heat with 1⁄2 tablespoon of the olive oil.
Cook the shells for 3 minutes, until the heads and shells change colour and go pink. Add the celery, fennel, fennel seeds, carrot, bay leaf, leek, white wine, and a pinch of salt.
Cook the mixture for 5 minutes, then add 750ml (25fl oz) of water. Bring the water to a simmer, skim off any foam, and leave the stock to cook for 30 minutes.
Strain the stock through a fine sieve into a bowl or jug, discard the prawn shells and cooked vegetables, and leave the strained stock to one side.

Heat 2 tablespoons of the remaining olive oil in a large, wide sauté pan with a tight-fitting lid over a high heat. Once hot, add the clams, mussels and peeled prawn flesh and cook for a couple of minutes, until the clams start to open.
Then add the puréed tomatoes and bring the liquid to a simmer.
Leave to simmer for 10 minutes, until the liquid has reduced by half, then stir in 4 ladlefuls of the prawn stock.

Season the monkfish, red mullet, and seabass or seabream fillets with salt and pepper and gently place these on top of the mixture in the pan. Place a lid on the pan and cook the fish gently for 2 minutes.

Then, add the garlic, parsley and chilli flakes and cook for a further 2 minutes, or until you can push a cocktail stick through the fish fillets without any resistance. Check the seasoning and adjust as necessary.
Toast the ciabatta slices, then rub with a garlic clove and drizzle them with olive oil. Serve the stew in hot bowls, with the toasted, garlicky ciabatta on the side for dipping.
